assertion.description: Recorded here for contrast, not because it is this disease. The same Hearing Loss Gene Curation Expert Panel rates GJB3's relationship with erythrokeratodermia variabilis Definitive, on a 2023 SOP v9 review - five years newer than the Disputed hearing-loss curation. dismech curates that disease separately as Erythrokeratodermia Variabilis.

selected_evidence.snippet: GJB3 | HGNC:4285 | erythrokeratodermia variabilis | MONDO:0017851 | AD | Definitive

assertion.name: ClinGen GJB3-nonsyndromic hearing loss gene-disease validity assertion
assertion.description: The ClinGen Hearing Loss Gene Curation Expert Panel classifies the autosomal dominant GJB3-nonsyndromic hearing loss relationship as Disputed, approved 2018-02-27. Its evidence summary is unusually explicit about why: the association rested on case-level data only, many reported variants are present at high frequency in population databases or have no evidence for pathogenicity, and only three variants had enough evidence to score.
assertion.notes:
The same expert panel classifies GJB3-erythrokeratodermia variabilis as Definitive. One gene, two curations by the same group, opposite verdicts - which is the cleanest possible demonstration that a gene's disease relationships have to be assessed one at a time.
The assertion's evidence summary cites PMID 12759707 among the publications in which the association was seen. Looked up at PubMed, that identifier is a 2003 Spanish-language editorial on smoking prevention in Anales del Sistema Sanitario de Navarra, so it is evidently a transcription error in the ClinGen record rather than a hearing-loss report. It is cited nowhere in this entry, and no attempt was made to guess which publication was intended.

selected_evidence.snippet: Multiple missense and nonsense variants have been reported in humans, however many of these variants are present in high frequency in population databases and/or have no evidence for pathogenicity.
